semantic_review: Neighbor-pressure sign follows minus carrier density times fixed-position potential derivative; both acceleration and product-rule speed-square terms are retained.
Independent Euler–Lagrange calculation from self and pair kinetic energy reproduces all coupled radial terms and their coefficients.
Polygon pitch is nearest-vertex distance; diagonal lengths and reciprocal sums are correct for 3,4,5.
The integrated symmetric trajectory conserves the retained leading-model pressure work; zero interaction recovers Rayleigh.
Fixed total pressure work changes each maximum radius rather than granting constant cavity size at higher site count.
Patterned/addressed optical allocation is explicitly separate from the broad Gaussian uniformity control, in EN and ZH.
Shared-fluid cluster solution is explicitly not a multiplier for 25 independent cells.
Material interface approximation excludes significant simultaneous mass transfer; finite sealed cells require actual pressure/volume/gauge boundaries.
Slender dynamics, exact geometric curvature, infinite-cylinder growth and finite-length jet arrival are not conflated.
The whole-radius disturbance time is labeled nonlinear extrapolation; the stated jet length is only about one fastest wavelength.
Early water-hammer scale is restricted by side/axial/receiver return times and finite momentum; equivalent rectangle is not claimed as a waveform.
Outgoing-wave energy bound is explicitly distinguished from contact traction and standing waves.
Paired physical qualifications, signs and numerical values inspected; no material EN/ZH contradiction found in reviewed sections.

concrete_issues.issue: The pressure-average bound uses the receiver normal contact-traction impulse. It needs pressure excess to equal the observed normal compressive traction, or a pressure-only impulse definition; nonnegative total normal traction alone does not guarantee a pressure-only bound when normal viscous stress is appreciable.
concrete_issues.recommended_fix: State negligible normal viscous stress in this observer control, or define the impulse budget explicitly as integral of observed pressure excess.

concrete_issues.issue: The finite slice starting equality uses A dz for a pointwise area; this is leading-order unless A is a slice average. The derived differential continuity law itself is correct.
concrete_issues.recommended_fix: Start with exact volume integral over [z,z+Δz], divide by positive Δz, then take Δz→0, or explicitly state the leading-order slice approximation.
